question.text: What role does value investing play as a remedy for behavioral biases in retirement planning?

answer.text: Value investing encourages buying stocks based on social media trends
Value investing is contrarian and helps reduce herd mentality; recency bias is better addressed through data-focused and scheduled process controls
Value investing means buying the most expensive stocks for perceived quality
Value investing has no relevance to behavioral bias remediation

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XVII (pp.91-92), value investing is described as contrarian and is highlighted as a way to avoid herd mentality. Recency bias is better managed through disciplined, data-focused processes and scheduled portfolio reviews rather than through value investing itself. The Trap: Value investing is not about chasing social-media trends or buying the most expensive names. It is also incorrect to extend it broadly as a direct cure for recency bias on the basis of the cited workbook pages. Note: For the equity portion of a retirement portfolio, pair a contrarian/value tilt with rule-based reviews and SIPs to dampen the influence of recent market noise.
